title: Unit – 4 : Session – 10 : SLO – 1  |  TCP Sockets in Python
sections: 1. c) Wait for connections — listen() puts the server socket into passive mode, queuing incoming connection requests.
1. bind() associates the socket with an IP address and a port number.
2. accept() returns a new socket object for the client connection (plus the client's address).
Typical server sequence: socket() → bind() → listen() → accept() → recv()/send() → close().
listen(backlog) only configures the queue; the actual handshake completes at accept().
